items.title: First Total Eclipse in Europe in Decades Turns Day to Night
items.summary: From Iceland to Spain, people flocked to viewing spots to see the moon completely block out the sun.

items.title: Ecuadorean Fishing Boats Hit by Mystery Attackers
items.summary: Ecuadorean crews plying the waters of the Pacific have been targeted by a mysterious outfit equipped with drones. Some sailors appear to have lost their lives.

items.title: How Nigel Farage Ended Up Running Against Count Binface in Clacton
items.summary: Nigel Farage forced a new election in his parliamentary seat after coming under pressure over his finances. His main challenger is Count Binface, a novelty candidate.

items.title: In Bali, a Quest to Restore the Sacred Glow of Fireflies
items.summary: The insects, revered in local culture, are disappearing for many reasons, including rapid development to cater to tourists.

items.title: Europeans, Braced for 5th Heat Wave of 2026, Have Had Enough
items.summary: With temperatures set to soar as high as 109 degrees Fahrenheit (43 Celsius) this week, Europeans and tourists say that summer in Europe has lost its appeal.

items.title: More Than 40 Dead After a Ferry Capsizes on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba
items.summary: The vessel was crowded far beyond capacity and was hit by strong waves, the police said. While dozens have been rescued, the search continues for an unknown number of missing people.

items.title: Trump Tariffs Force Some Canadian Companies to Move South of the Border
items.summary: If President Trump moves ahead with 50 percent tariffs on a wide range of Canadian products later this month, some companies may only survive by relocating to the United States.

items.title: A Space Expert Hoped to Use the Eclipse as Science Class. The D.J.s Had Other Plans.
items.summary: Mar Carretero-Castrillo, an astrophysicist, returned to her remote village in Spain to be in the path of totality. Hundreds of partygoers came too.

items.title: Thailand Halts New Gun Permits After Mass Shooting at a School
items.summary: It remains to be seen how far the government will go to tighten gun control in the country, which has experienced a string of high-profile shootings in recent years.

items.title: Zambia Election: President Hichilema Faces Backlash Ahead of Vote
items.summary: President Hakainde Hichilema was elected five years ago, promising to protect civil liberties in his copper-rich African nation. Now, he’s accused of trampling on them.

items.title: Treasury Scales Back Scrutiny of U.S. Shell Companies
items.summary: The Trump administration will not enforce reporting requirements of the 2021 Corporate Transparency Act, which was intended to crack down on money laundering.

items.title: Forbes Fired Top Editor After Discovering He Received Secret $6 Million Payment
items.summary: Randall Lane, the magazine’s chief content officer, received the money from the founder of Shook Research, which has worked with Forbes on content about wealth advisers.

items.title: Prediction Firms Are Flagging Insider Traders. Many Will Not Face Charges.
items.summary: The agency that polices the industry does not have the staffing, the legal tools or the will to broadly crack down on wagers that are easily manipulated, experts say.

items.title: Ted Decker, CEO of Home Depot, Is Taking Medical Leave
items.summary: Ted Decker is expected to return in a few months, and two executives have been appointed to oversee his duties in the interim.

items.title: Gulf Oil Giants Are Spending Billions to Build Ways Around Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Even if a cease-fire materializes, Gulf exporters recognize that relying strictly on the Strait of Hormuz is a risk they can no longer take.

items.title: Consumer Debt Data Shows ‘Overall’ Health Amid Persisting Divides
items.summary: Homeowners with low fixed-rate mortgages lead a resilient picture of the economy. But many consumers are frustrated with declining real wages and other loans.

items.title: Will Paramount’s Brinkmanship Work?
items.summary: The media company’s leader, David Ellison, is threatening to pull the company out of California in the face of a lawsuit by states seeking to block its big deal.

items.title: Thrive Holdings, A.I.-Focused Buyer of Service Firms, Raises $2 Billion
items.summary: The company, Thrive Holdings, acquires businesses to infuse them with artificial intelligence and drew interest from backers like SoftBank.

items.title: Benign Inflation Data Offers Reprieve to Fed as It Weighs Rate Increase
items.summary: The latest Consumer Price Index report helped to reinforce the patient approach adopted by many officials at the Federal Reserve about raising rates, but it has not resolved the debate altogether.

items.title: The labor market slowed as employers grew wary of hiring.
How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
items.summary: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

items.title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
items.summary: A co-founder of xAI is going all in on building open-source artificial intelligence so that “anyone can control and shape A.I. for their own needs.”

items.title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom

items.title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
items.summary: As Waymo deploys more driverless cars to 15 U.S. cities and counting, its vehicles keep encountering new and unexpected situations that they have no script to handle.

items.title: 3 Ex-Georgia Deputies Used Flock Cameras to Stalk People, Sheriff Says
items.summary: The former Bibb County deputies were arrested this week amid a growing national debate over Flock cameras, which can be found on roads in every state but Alaska.

items.title: Driver Sets Record for Hydrogen-Powered Vehicle at More Than 406 M.P.H.
items.summary: Andy Green, a 64-year-old retired Royal Air Force pilot from Britain, was already the only person to break the sound barrier on land. “The ground comes at you very, very quickly,” he said.

items.title: Spotify Will Label A.I. Artists and Avoid Promoting Them
items.summary: The new label, which will begin to be applied next month, is an effort by the streaming service to be more transparent about A.I.-generated music on its app.

items.title: Brad Lightcap, a Top OpenAI Executive, Steps Down
items.summary: Brad Lightcap, a longtime leader, said he was starting a new venture. His exit from the artificial intelligence company is the latest in a series there.

items.title: Meta Unveils an Open Version of Its Most Powerful A.I. Model
items.summary: The release of Muse Glimmer, a model that can be freely downloaded and modified, is likely to intensify a debate over whether A.I. should be restricted.
